meta.status: Five questions below are answered with evidence. Ten remain open, and each one names the specific artefact that would close it. Nothing here is a forecast.
meta.rule: A question moves to 'answered' only when the answer has a source link. An answer of 'we cannot know yet' is a legitimate answer and is recorded as such.

questions.question: Does each submitted link actually land on the product the owner meant to send readers to?
questions.what_we_have: All five links resolve to live listings, and each arrival ASIN and title was transcribed (P-01..P-05: 3 Air Fryers and 2 Meat Thermometers).
questions.what_is_missing: The owner's intended ASIN. Every submitted path code is 9 characters; every ASIN observed on arrival is 10. That is evidence the codes are short-link slugs, not identifiers, so the intended product cannot be read off the link itself.
questions.how_to_close: In the Associates dashboard, open SiteStripe for each product and copy the tagged link for the exact ASIN intended, then record both values side by side.
questions.blocking: yes — every product claim downstream depends on it

questions.question: Why did P-04 fail to resolve on earlier checks, and what does it point to now?
questions.what_we_have: Earlier automated requests to https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 hit Amazon's /checkpoint/continue interstitial. Two independent re-verifications on 2026-11-20 resolved it directly to ASIN B0DHZTCNR5 (ThermoMaven 1 Sec Professional Digital Meat Thermometer).
questions.what_is_missing: Confirmation from the owner that B0DHZTCNR5 is the intended product, and replacement of the intermittent short link with a direct validated Special Link.
questions.how_to_close: Confirm B0DHZTCNR5 in the Associates dashboard and issue a validated Special Link (S-02).
questions.answer: P-04 resolved on 2026-11-20 to ASIN B0DHZTCNR5 (ThermoMaven 1 Sec Professional Digital Meat Thermometer, category Thermometers & Timers > Meat). Earlier failures were Amazon /checkpoint/continue interstitials, confirming that link.amazon redirects can gate automated or repeat fetches intermittently (FLG-004).
questions.blocking: no — destination observed; owner confirmation of intended ASIN sits under Q-01

questions.question: Are the clicks actually attributed to shopnow047c-20?
questions.what_we_have: The tracking ID was supplied in the brief. Nothing on any arrived-at page showed a tag parameter.
questions.what_is_missing: Evidence that the link the server serves carries the tag, and a click that then shows up in the Associates click report.
questions.how_to_close: One test click on the owner's own device, then check the Associates click report for that day. That is the only permitted source for this number.
questions.blocking: yes — without it the site can send traffic that earns nothing

questions.question: Should the site show prices?
questions.what_we_have: Amazon's Program Policies allow showing price and availability only where Amazon serves the link carrying that data, or where it arrives via Creators API or PA API (SRC-02).
questions.what_is_missing: A decision, and if the answer is yes, API credentials.
questions.how_to_close: Either apply for API access and render Amazon-served prices only, or keep prices off the site. Both are compliant; a scraped price is not.
questions.answer: No price, star rating, review count or stock status appears anywhere on this site, because neither permitted data path is connected.
questions.blocking: no — the site is compliant without prices

questions.question: Is the disclosure in the right place?
questions.what_we_have: The Operating Agreement requires the exact statement on the site (SRC-01). The FTC says a footer-only disclosure is easy to miss and that proximity to the recommendation matters (SRC-03).
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing structural. What remains is a legal review of the wording around it, which this build cannot perform.
questions.how_to_close: A human review against SRC-01, SRC-03 and 16 CFR Part 255 (SRC-04). The placement itself is already above the fold on every page and repeated in the footer.
questions.answer: The required sentence sits in a strip under the masthead above the fold on every page, and repeats in the footer. Every product card and product record repeats the affiliate note beside the outbound link.

questions.question: Two of the five links (P-04 and P-05) are meat thermometers, not air fryers. Should the site stay a two-category publication?
questions.what_we_have: Amazon's category breadcrumbs put P-01, P-02 and P-03 under Air Fryers and both P-04 (ThermoMaven instant-read) and P-05 (CHEF iQ wireless 3-probe) under Thermometers & Timers > Meat.
questions.what_is_missing: The owner's long-term niche strategy — keep both Air Fryers and Meat Thermometers as complementary categories, or narrow exclusively to one.
questions.how_to_close: One sentence from the owner (see S-08). Until then the site treats both categories cleanly with dedicated category pages (Air Fryers and Meat Thermometers) and a USDA-sourced thermometer guide.
questions.blocking: no — handled cleanly via two dedicated categories

questions.question: Which guide topics are worth expanding next?
questions.what_we_have: Seven question-shaped guides across air fryers, meat thermometers, meal prep and seasonal hosting, clearly labelled as editorial hypotheses.
questions.what_is_missing: Any search data at all. No Search Console property, no impressions, no query list, no click data.
questions.how_to_close: Verify the property in Search Console, submit the sitemap, wait for impressions, then export the query report and pick the next topic from measured queries.
questions.blocking: no — but writing more guides before this is guessing

questions.question: Who is the author, and why should a reader trust them?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. There is no named person, no credentials, no first-hand testing.
questions.what_is_missing: A real byline and a real basis for it. This is the single largest trust gap on the site and cannot be automated away.
questions.how_to_close: A named editor with a short, accurate bio. Claiming testing that did not happen would breach both the FTC guides and the Operating Agreement, so the bio must describe what the writer actually did.
questions.blocking: partly — it limits how much authority the guides can claim

questions.question: What is the actual commission rate for these categories?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. The rate card sits behind an Associates sign-in.
questions.what_is_missing: The owner's own rate card for Home & Kitchen small appliances and kitchen gadgets.
questions.how_to_close: Read it in the Associates dashboard and record it. It is deliberately blank here rather than copied from a blog.
questions.blocking: no — but no revenue estimate is possible without it, so none is given

questions.question: Is the analytics endpoint live, and is it lawful to switch on?
questions.what_we_have: Five defined events, an inert client in assets/js/analytics.js, and a self-hosted Node collector in server/collect.js.
questions.what_is_missing: A first-party host for the collector (GitHub Pages is static), a formal privacy notice, a retention period, and a decision on consent for visitors in jurisdictions that require it.
questions.how_to_close: Publish the privacy notice first, deploy the collector on a first-party host, then enable the beacon. The order matters.
questions.blocking: yes, for measurement — the site works without it

questions.question: Can this site be indexed at all, given the repository path?
questions.what_we_have: The site is served from /Affil1/ on github.io. All internal links resolve within that subpath, and sitemap.xml and feed.xml list every canonical URL.
questions.what_is_missing: Verification that the sitemap has been submitted in Google Search Console and that pages are actually being crawled.
questions.how_to_close: Search Console verification, then sitemap submission, then check coverage after a few days.
questions.blocking: no — but nothing will rank reliably until it happens

questions.question: Does the site make any claim it cannot support?
questions.what_we_have: Every page is machine-checked for banned patterns: no price figure, no star rating, no review count, no stock status, no superlative, no test claim. Food-safety temperatures are sourced directly from USDA FSIS (SRC-06, SRC-07).
questions.what_is_missing: A human read for tone and implication — a checker cannot catch a sentence that is technically true but suggests more.
questions.how_to_close: Read the guides and product pages once with the question 'what would a sceptical reader infer?'
questions.answer: No page claims testing, ranking or a winner. Every product page states plainly that the product was not tested, and every food-safety temperature cites USDA FSIS directly.

questions.question: What happens if the owner never supplies the missing account data?
questions.what_we_have: A site that is compliant and verified across all five product destinations, with honest guides and zero invented prices or ratings.
questions.what_is_missing: A decision about how long to wait.
questions.how_to_close: This is an owner decision, not a research one. The site is built to be safe to leave running in this state indefinitely.
questions.answer: Nothing on the site breaks. It stays accurate because it claims only what was verified. The cost of the missing data is opportunity, not correctness.
questions.evidence: Internal build verification (tools/check.py) — stated plainly so it is not mistaken for an external citation.

questions.question: Are the supplied links Special Links in the sense the agreement means?
questions.what_we_have: All five resolve to live Amazon listings. None showed a tag parameter on arrival.
questions.what_is_missing: Confirmation that each is tagged with shopnow047c-20. The agreement requires Special Links to use the assigned Associates ID (SRC-02).
questions.how_to_close: Re-issue each destination as a tagged link from SiteStripe, test one click, and replace the outbound URL after recording both the old and new value.
questions.blocking: yes — this is the difference between a link and a commission

questions.question: Is there any traffic, and where would it come from?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. No analytics running, no Search Console, no referral data.
questions.how_to_close: Turn on measurement (Q-10) and Search Console verification (Q-11) before assuming any channel works.
questions.blocking: no — but every revenue assumption depends on it
